# bif-app v0.1.0-alpha.4 — OSS-focused desktop UI

Independent desktop wrapper based on the open-source Bifrost AI Gateway by Maxim. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Maxim.

Windows x64 portable, using the Microsoft WebView2 runtime already installed on your PC. No installer or bundled WebView2 runtime.

## Changes

The desktop build now hides audited Enterprise-only placeholder navigation and upgrade prompts while keeping the original Bifrost UI and all OSS backend behavior.

- Hides Enterprise placeholder entries for Circuit Breaker, Alerting, enterprise governance/permissions, Guardrails, Edge Control, Cluster Config and Adaptive Routing, including sidebar search results.
- Hides the audited Enterprise observability connector selectors, the production-setup demo card, the API Keys scoped-access promotion, the Prompt Deployments promotion and Enterprise-only feature-flag display rows.
- Preserves providers, ordinary routing and Complexity Router, logging/usage, MCP, plugins, Virtual Keys, Teams, Customers, OSS authentication guidance and prompt editing. OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and Maxim connectors remain available.
- Old direct links to placeholder pages show a neutral unavailable message. Existing routes, APIs, permissions, database and business configuration are unchanged.
- This is a compile-time desktop presentation option. Ordinary Bifrost Web builds retain their original UI behavior by default.

The exact hide/retain list and upstream maintenance guidance are included in `OSS_UI_PLAN.md`. Upstream UI changes are isolated from desktop build/test integration in Git history. Existing custom IP/localhost settings from alpha.3 are retained.

## Upgrade

Quit the old version using its tray **Quit** menu, extract the complete ZIP into a new folder, and double-click `bif-app.exe`. Keep the sidecar and accompanying files together. Existing Bifrost data, desktop network settings and Windows Credential Manager key are preserved.

The default API is `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`. Use **Copy API Base URL** in the tray for the actual configured endpoint.

## Validation

The release commit is built and tested on clean Windows CI:

- Five browser cases for the ordinary production UI and five for the desktop production UI: complete audited navigation, search/keyboard navigation, connectors, auth guidance, direct routes, feature flags and real temporary prompt CRUD/editor controls.
- Fourteen Rust unit/helper tests and two real-sidecar integration tests, including OpenAI-compatible requests to a local mock provider without paid credentials.
- Launch of the extracted portable host, original UI readiness, loopback listener, single instance, crash reaping, and restart with existing data/key/port.
- Actual Desktop Settings WebView validation, rollback, persistence and IPv4/IPv6/localhost endpoint behavior.
- Ordinary `bifrost-http` build.

Unsigned alpha. No paid provider calls or new physical Windows 11 session are included in this release's validation. Interactive tray coverage is documented in `VALIDATION.md`; this release's hosted CI does not automate tray menu clicks. Portable only; no installer was produced.
